transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Ever since the car accident last week, I keep reliving it over and over in my head, even when I’m trying to work or relax, and I can’t seem to shut it off. It feels like it's completely taking over my life, and I just don't know how to make it stop.
Have these distressing memories and feelings been constant every day since the accident, or have you noticed them starting to ease up at all over the last week?

They have been completely constant and haven't let up at all over the six days since the crash. It is just exhausting because I haven't had a single moment of relief, and I feel completely overwhelmed by it.
Have you ever experienced similar symptoms of reliving a traumatic event that lasted for more than a month after a scary experience in the past?
No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. This is the very first time I've had these kinds of reactions, and it's completely new to me.
Are you finding yourself avoiding things that remind you of the accident, such as driving, riding in a car, or even talking about what happened?

Yes, I've been going completely out of my way to avoid any reminders. I refuse to get behind the wheel, and I immediately change the subject if someone mentions road trips or turn off songs from that festival. If my husband even suggests taking the highway, I just shut down and insist we stay home.
Have you also been having trouble sleeping, or have you felt constantly on edge and easily startled since the accident occurred?

Yes, I feel incredibly on edge and jump out of my skin at any sudden noise, like a door slamming or a dropped book. My heart starts racing and I'll shake for several minutes afterward, though sleep itself hasn't been the main issue I've noticed. I'm just constantly on high alert and find myself snapping at my husband and my students because of it.
Did these feelings of reliving the event and being on edge start immediately within minutes or hours of the accident, or did they take a few days to develop?
They started almost immediately, pretty much as soon as I got home that night. It really didn't take any time at all to develop, and they've been happening nonstop ever since.
Since the accident, have you felt emotionally numb, or experienced a sense of detachment from yourself or your surroundings, as if you are in a dream?

Yes, I feel completely flat and disconnected, like I'm watching someone else's life and can't feel any real joy or warmth even when my niece sends me her drawings. I also keep getting this weird, floaty feeling where my surroundings look far away and unreal, and it feels like I'm watching myself from just over my shoulder instead of actually being in my own body.
Even though sleep hasn't been your main concern, have you experienced any vivid nightmares or distressing dreams specifically about the accident?

No, I haven't really had any vivid nightmares or distressing dreams about the accident. My main struggle has just been those intense, intrusive memories popping up constantly while I'm awake during the day.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with severe intrusive memories, avoidance, hyperarousal, and dissociative symptoms (depersonalization and derealization) following a car accident 6 days ago. Because the symptoms have persisted for only 6 days (less than the 1-month threshold typically required for PTSD) and began immediately after the trauma, the presentation is consistent with an acute stress reaction (F43.0) rather than post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1).
